correctness.rationale: Every target degree has a parity restriction to \(2^{d-1}\) Walsh characters. At degree \(d+2\), the full sign-character projection is \(x_1\cdots x_d\) times a diagonal quadratic, whose Laplacian zero forces coefficient sum zero and whose corner values vanish. All other characters are generated by explicit products of disjoint two- and three-variable solid harmonics; at \(d\) and \(d+4\) the top character and cases with two complementary variables are handled separately. The exhaustive symbolic cases cover all integers \(d\ge3\). Exact Gegenbauer-Walsh computations for dimensions 3 through 10 corroborate the theorem but do not prove the infinite-dimensional parameter range.

value.rationale: The natural antipodal vertex-data space has \(2^{d-1}\) degrees of freedom. For every integer \(d\ge3\), the exact-degree harmonic sampling ranks at \(d,d+2,d+4\) show a universal, precisely one-character loss followed by full recovery. This identifies an exact interpolation obstruction and complete local rank pattern with explicit interpolating polynomials, relevant to symmetry-resolved harmonic sampling rather than an arbitrary finite calculation.
